negative_findings.description: No Diebold Nixdorf press release, case study, or partner-locator entry naming Montenegro or a Montenegrin bank was found, in either English or Serbian queries.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two searches (en and sr-flavoured) returned only Diebold Nixdorf deployments in Belgium, the Nordics, Antarctica and unnamed 'top-10' institutions. Absence is unverified, not proven — the ME market may be served indirectly through resellers such as Printec or Payten rather than by direct DN contracts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If DN has no direct ME presence, the ATM hardware/service competition in Montenegro is effectively a reseller/integrator contest (Payten, Printec, Euronet), which changes who the real competitor set is.

negative_findings.description: No Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Finastra, Backbase, Sopra Banking, BPC SmartVista or OpenWay Way4 customer story naming a Montenegrin bank was located.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple vendor-scoped and platform-scoped searches returned only generic product/comparison pages and non-ME references (Openbank, Commerce Bank, Tsesnabank).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests the ME core-banking and card-processing installed base is held by regional vendors (ASEE/Asseco, Payten) and by group-level systems imported from parent banks (NLB, OTP, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat), rather than by direct tier-1 global core vendor contracts. This should be tested against bank annual reports and parent-group IT disclosures.

negative_findings.description: No public partner-locator or reseller-directory entry for Montenegro was found for any of the global vendors in scope (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Temenos, Oracle, Thales, IDEMIA).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for partner locators returned only Mastercard's Move partner directory (not ME-specific). Vendor partner locators may exist behind JS-driven interfaces that plain web search does not index.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Partner locators are usually the densest single mapping of a global vendor to its local channel; not finding them via search means they need direct browser-based interrogation rather than search-engine discovery.

negative_findings.description: No vendor named yet for Montenegro's TIPS Clone instant-payments build; the supplier hypothesis (Nexi/SIA, Bankart) is unconfirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: CBCG material identifies Banca d'Italia and the World Bank as counterparties and a mid-2026 target, and an open RFB for 'TIPS Clone Connectivity Services', but names no technology supplier.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The largest payments-infrastructure programme in the market currently has no attributable vendor; whoever wins the connectivity and bank-side adaptation work gains a durable position with all ME banks.

negative_findings.description: No Worldline, Nexi, Ingenico or Verifone page referencing Montenegro operations, an ME merchant-acquiring business, or an ME terminal contract was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned only pan-European market-structure material and the Worldline/Ingenico merger documentation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Indicates ME acquiring is bank-owned and locally serviced rather than outsourced to a pan-European acquirer — a structurally different competitive landscape from Croatia or Serbia.

negative_findings.description: Serbian/Montenegrin-language searching produced far fewer vendor-side results than English, because international vendors publish ME wins in English on their global sites, not in sr.
negative_findings.result_summary: sr queries ('Crna Gora banka implementirala rješenje dobavljač saopštenje', 'Asseco SEE Crna Gora Podgorica banka projekat') returned bank and central-bank pages rather than vendor pages; the productive sr surfaces were vendor local sites (euronetatms.me), bank product pages, and bankar.me.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: for vendor-side evidence English is the primary language, while sr is needed to reach vendor local subsidiaries, job ads and bank-side technology fingerprints. Collection must run both, with different source lists.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor partner-locator and 'find a partner' tools were not interrogated directly — they are typically JavaScript applications that web search cannot index.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Drive the partner locators of Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Temenos, Oracle, Thales and IDEMIA with a headless browser, querying country=Montenegro, and capture the underlying JSON endpoints for repeatable collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Card-personalisation and identity vendors (Thales, IDEMIA, Giesecke+Devrient, Veridos) and cash-handling vendors (Glory, CIMA) were not searched against Montenegro in this pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side evidence hidden in bank parent-group IT disclosures (NLB, OTP/CKB, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat, Adriatic Bank owners) was not covered — group-level vendor contracts often determine the ME subsidiary's stack.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search parent-group annual reports, IT procurement notices and vendor press releases naming the parent group, then check whether the ME subsidiary is in scope.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor conference and roadshow material (Asseco/Payten SEE user conferences, Mastercard/Visa regional events, Sibos/Money Motion/Fintech Adria agendas) frequently names ME bank clients in speaker bios and session titles, and was not searched.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run vendor newsroom crawls with explicit date filtering for 2023 onward, and prioritise the TIPS Clone award notices expected around 2026 as the freshest vendor-attribution event.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Let the deterministic liveness pass resolve them; where a path 404s, re-discover the newsroom from the vendor homepage rather than dropping the vendor.

brief: Montenegro's vendor-side evidence is concentrated in two regional suppliers rather than the global tier-1s: Payten (Asseco Group) publishes both a named ME implementation (SoftPOS/MojPOS at Hipotekarna banka, 2022) and a quantified installed base (present since 2006, >350 ATMs and >7,000 POS maintained, partnerships with nine of eleven banks), while ASEE publishes a named core-banking win (ASEBA PUB 2000 at Ziraat Bank Montenegro, live July 2015) and maintains a Podgorica entity. Printec and Euronet both run local Montenegro presences with their own country sites, Euronet's in Serbian. No Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Temenos, Oracle, Finastra, BPC, OpenWay, Worldline or Nexi page naming Montenegro was found in this pass, which is itself a finding: the ME market appears to be reached through regional integrators and parent-bank group systems rather than direct global-vendor contracts. The richest forward-looking vendor-attribution surface is the CBCG's World Bank-financed TIPS Clone programme, whose open tenders and forthcoming award notices will name suppliers before any vendor press release does.
